newsitem.title: MOLDOVA: SOCCER-RAVANELLI LEADS ITALY TO TRIUMPH IN MOLDOVA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RAVANELLI LEADS ITALY TO TRIUMPH IN MOLDOVA.

text.p: Fabrizio Ravanelli scored twice and Pierluigi Casiraghi added another as Italy overcame a case of defensive jitters to defeat Moldova 3-1 in their World Cup European group two opener on Saturday.
The win was important for Italy and embattled coach Arrigo Sacchi, made a scapegoat for his team's shock elimination from Euro 96.
But victory was no easy task as the hosts proved far more aggressive than Sacchi -- who began the match with a bold attacking trident -- had imagined.
"They were simply getting to the balls before we were and when you can't even get to it first, well, what can you do?" Sacchi said.
"I'm pleased we won but clearly for this team it's still `work in progress'."

Despite being outnumbered in midfield, Italy went ahead in the eighth minute when Middlesbrough striker Ravanelli curved a free-kick from the edge of the area just over the outstretched arms of goalkeeper Denis Romanenko.
But Moldova struck back three minutes later when midfielder Alexandru Curtianu exploited a defensive blunder by Juventus stopper Ciro Ferrara and blasted the ball past a helpless Francesco Toldo.

The hosts, playing with five midfielders to Italy's three, neutralised the Italians who continued to be nervous in defence until Sacchi remedied the problem by inserting midfielder Angelo Di Livio for Chiesa after the interval.
Juventus's Di Livio showed his class in the 68th minute, serving up a perfect cross which Lazio's Casiraghi headed in for his 11th international goal.
Ravanelli then provided insurance from the spot three minutes from time after Casiraghi was hauled down in the penalty area.
